courses.title: Structural Geology
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, six hours. Recommended: course 61. Planar and linear structures at different scales in sedimentary, metamorphic, and igneous rocks. Faults and folds, their description, classification, and kinematic and dynamic analysis. Deformation, strength, fracture, and rheological properties of rocks. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.description: Tutorial, two hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Supervised individual research or investigation under guidance of faculty mentor. Culminating paper or project required. May be repeated for credit. Individual contract required. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.description: (Same as Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences M71.) Lecture, four hours; outside computing study, six to 10 hours. Introduction to writing programs, visualization of geoscience data, and comparison with models. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Principles of Geomorphology
courses.description: (Formerly numbered 100.) Lecture, three hours; reading period, one hour. Requisite: course 1. Study of processes that shape world’s landforms, with emphasis on weathering, mass movement and fluvial erosion, transport, deposition; energy and material transfers; space and time considerations. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Climatology
courses.description: (Formerly numbered 104.) Lecture, three hours; reading period, one hour. Designed for juniors/seniors. Examination of many relations between climate and world of man. Application of basic energy budget concepts to microclimates of relevance to ecosystems of agriculture, animals, man, and urban places. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Hydrology
courses.description: (Formerly numbered 105.) Lecture, three hours. Requisites: course 116, Statistics 12. Role of water in geographic systems: hydrologic phenomena in relation to climate, landforms, soils, vegetation, and cultural processes and impacts on landscape. Field projects required. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Health and Global Environment
courses.description: (Formerly numbered 125.) Lecture, three hours; reading period, one hour. Impact of environment and lifestyle on individual health examined from geographical perspective, with examples from both developed and developing countries. P/NP or letter grading.
